page: Amazon Web Services r5n.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. It does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and does not feature hardware acceleration GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and high-throughput memory performance. The instance achieved 81307.18 on multi-core stress-ng, a 55814.83 PassMark CPU score, and strong performance in Clang compilation and ray tracing. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high bandwidth, reaching 4505.69 GB/sec for small cached reads and 220.43 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Key-value operations reflect this capability, with Redis SET throughput reaching 73.84 million operations per second and static web throughput exceeding 45 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics are lower, with weak single-core stress-ng and compression results, along with poor token generation rates in LLM text generation benchmarks.

The hardware configuration trades single-threaded execution speed for extensive memory capacity and multi-threaded scaling. Without local NVMe storage, persistent high-throughput I/O depends entirely on network storage channels leveraging the 100 Gbps network capacity. The high density of 768.0 GB RAM alongside dedicated compute cores delivers qualitative efficiency for memory-bound workloads by consolidating distributed clusters. The instance fits large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, memory-intensive enterprise caching layers, large distributed data processing systems, and parallel compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores and 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. It delivers 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but contains no bundled local storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal exceptional multi-core performance, robust memory bandwidth reaching 220.43 GB/sec on uncached reads, and 73.84 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution metrics and LLM token generation speeds are comparatively lower. The platform offers high resource density for workloads requiring vast RAM pools and high network throughput, making it well matched for in-memory database deployments, enterprise caching grids, large-scale memory-resident analytics, and distributed software build infrastructure.
